summary: Aurora DataHub — embedding index checkpoint drift after maintenance leading to stale search results (customer escalation)
description:
Issue summary: Aurora DataHub reported a burst of stale/low-recall embedding search results following a scheduled control-plane maintenance window. Customer saw query vectors matched to previous index snapshots causing mismatches with recently ingested content.

Impact: Production search for Aurora DataHub customers returned stale embeddings for a subset of queries (~5-8% of traffic for the tenant), causing incorrect recommendations and a measurable drop in user engagement metrics. Customer escalated to enterprise SLA channel and requested immediate rollback or mitigation.

Environment: prod (us-east-1) using Redwood hosted inference + managed embeddings indexing (open-embed-2.5 quantized variant enabled). Maintenance window completed at 2026-03-10T11:05Z. First customer reports at ~2026-03-10T11:20Z.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Use Aurora DataHub test tenant and submit ingestion job A (document batch) with embedding write-through enabled. 2) Run search queries Q1..Q10 before and after a checkpoint. 3) Observe that post-maintenance queries sometimes return vector matches from checkpoint N-1 despite successful acknowledgement of ingest. Intermittent and not 100% reproducible in our sandbox; appears related to checkpoint/compaction ordering during maintenance.

Logs/Observations: - Control-plane maintenance altered the index checkpointting job run order across two nodes. - Index compaction logs show occasional "checkpoint-swap" events where the active pointer moved back to previous snapshot for tenant aurora-datahub-org-17. - KV cache hit metrics for embeddings show unexpected evictions at 11:10Z. - No 5xxs or throttles reported; request success rates unaffected, but similarity scores and top-k returned differ.

Preliminary mitigation applied: - Forced a recheckpoint of Aurora DataHub's active embedding index (manual compaction) at 2026-03-10T12:05Z which restored expected results for ~70% of impacted queries. - We put a temporary routing policy to pin the tenant to the node that completed compaction successfully while we investigate cross-node checkpoint pointers.

Requested by customer: full validation that all recently ingested documents are present in the active index, audit evidence for their SLA credits, and a permanent fix to avoid checkpoint pointer regressions during maintenance.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: A race in the control-plane checkpoint-swap logic (introduced during recent maintenance orchestration change) allowed the active index pointer to briefly revert to a previous snapshot when two compaction/merge jobs overlapped across replicas. Evidence: checkpoint-swap log entries at 11:06-11:12Z showing pointer moves, KV eviction spike at 11:09Z, and correlation with maintenance job ordering. Repro: Simulated overlapping compaction jobs in staging and observed pointer revert in 1/25 runs. Mitigation: 'pin routing' and manual recheckpoint; long-term fix is a CAS guard and post-maintenance reconciliation job. Linked INT-4021 for orchestration config hardening.
resolution_notes:
Workaround: manual recheckpoint and temporary tenant-node pinning restored service for majority of queries. Permanent fix: merged patch (PR 2190) adds compare-and-swap guards and a verification pass after any maintenance that touches compaction/checkpointing. Rollout plan: canary in us-east-1 non-prod (2026-03-12), staged prod rollout (2026-03-13 through 2026-03-14) with enhanced monitoring.

Customer communication: provided audit bundle and step-by-step explanation of root cause. Billing ops engaged to evaluate SLA credit request.

Follow-ups (action items):
- INT-4021: orchestration config defaults to disable overlapping compactions for single-tenant critical namespaces (owner: SRE).
- Add automated per-tenant index-consistency checks to Redwood Optimize (owner: Applied ML infra).
- Update runbook for maintenance window choreography and include pointer reconciliation checklist (owner: On-call SRE).
follow_up_items: Runbook update: maintenance pointer reconciliation checklist
sla_impact: Production search degraded for Aurora DataHub tenant for ~3 hours (11:05Z-14:10Z) with impact to a subset of queries. Enterprise SLA channel engaged; billing ops evaluating credit.
